journal.title: Before the first frame
journal.excerpt: A few starting points for planning a portrait with an editorial point of view.
journal.body:
Start with what the photograph is for. A personal portrait, a portfolio image and a photograph for a website can ask for different things.

Bring a small set of references. Notice the light, mood and setting you respond to, rather than trying to reproduce another person's expression or pose.

Think about wardrobe as shape and texture. A few intentional options are easier to work with than a suitcase of unrelated looks.

Leave room for the location. Los Angeles offers a wide range of visual settings; the right one supports the image you want to make.

If you would like to plan a session, get in touch with your ideas and references.

faq.question: Where do you photograph?
faq.answer: I am based in Los Angeles. Sessions take place in the city and surrounding areas; travel can be discussed for a specific project.

faq.question: I have never been photographed professionally. Is that okay?
faq.answer: Yes. Portrait sessions include direction and posing guidance. We can discuss the mood and purpose of the photographs before the shoot.

faq.question: Is retouching included?
faq.answer: Professional retouching is available. The image selection and retouching scope are agreed directly before booking. For standalone retouching, get in touch with your images and requirements.

faq.question: How do I book?
faq.answer: Email dzamorskaya@icloud.com or send a message to @zam.photo on Instagram. Tell me the type of shoot, your preferred timing and any ideas or references.

faq.question: What is the difference between headshots and personal branding?
faq.answer: Headshots focus on a clear portrait for professional or casting use. Personal branding develops a wider visual library: portraits, working moments, lifestyle images and different formats for your business.

faq.question: Can brands request a custom quote?
faq.answer: Yes. Send your brief, deliverables, timeline and intended image usage. Production, licensing and post-production can then be scoped for the project.
